title.en: Make constraints sound like engineering inputs, not excuses.
title.zh: 把约束说成工程输入，而不是借口。

subtitle.en: Agentic systems are loops, not single calls. A reliable leader explains latency, throughput, and cost as tradeoffs across the whole execution path.
subtitle.zh: Agentic 系统是循环，不是单次调用。可靠的负责人会把延迟、吞吐和成本解释为整条执行路径上的权衡。

audience: GenAI FDE · AI platform engineer · Technical Account Manager

scenario.customer: The prototype was fine, but after real traffic increased, latency got worse and cost became hard to justify.
scenario.weakResponse: We can use a faster model and increase quota.
scenario.reliableResponse: Increasing quota may be part of the answer, but I would first map the end-to-end execution path: model calls, tool calls, retrieval, serialization, retries, and any sequential steps. Otherwise we may scale the expensive part without removing the actual bottleneck.

principle.en: Optimize the loop, not the headline model.
principle.zh: 优化整个循环，而不是只盯着模型名称。

title.en: Use tradeoff language to project maturity.
title.zh: 用权衡语言体现成熟度。

anchor.quote: A cheaper call can be a false economy if it increases retries, tool calls, or human review.

concept.en: False economy is a compact way to say that saving money locally can create higher system cost later.
concept.zh: False economy 很精炼：局部省钱，可能导致系统总成本更高。

intent.zh: 回应只优化模型的想法。

examples.line: A faster model may help, but the bottleneck may sit in the orchestration path rather than the model call itself.

why.en: You broaden the frame without dismissing the customer's idea.
why.zh: 你扩大问题框架，但没有否定客户想法。

examples.line: Cost per call is useful, but cost per successful task is the metric that will change the business case.

why.en: You move from component thinking to outcome thinking.
why.zh: 你从组件成本转向结果成本。

examples.line: Instrumentation is not overhead here; it is what lets us distinguish a scaling problem from a design problem.

why.en: Not overhead reframes invisible engineering work as decision infrastructure.
why.zh: Not overhead 把不可见工程工作重新定义成决策基础设施。

lines.line: Before we scale, I would like to understand whether we are constrained by model latency, retrieval latency, tool latency, or sequential orchestration.

why.en: You sound responsible because you name the possible bottlenecks before spending money.
why.zh: 你先说出可能瓶颈，再花钱，听起来很负责任。

intent.zh: 把架构和用户体验连起来。

lines.line: The user does not experience our architecture; they experience the total wait time across the loop.

why.zh: 这句话简单，也适合对高层说。

lines.line: The question is not only how many tokens we spend, but how much reliable work each token buys us.

why.en: You turn cost into productivity, not austerity.
why.zh: 你把成本讨论转成生产力讨论，而不是单纯节省。

intent.zh: 给出有纪律的优化顺序。

lines.line: I would first measure, then remove unnecessary sequential steps, then evaluate model and caching choices.

why.en: The sequence is calm: measure, simplify, then substitute.
why.zh: 顺序很稳：先测量，再简化，再替换。

lines.line: We can reduce latency, but I would not do it by making the system less verifiable.

why.en: You establish a non-negotiable boundary around trust.
why.zh: 你围绕信任建立了不可牺牲的边界。

prompt.en: Practice explaining scaling tradeoffs with executive calm.
prompt.zh: 练习用高层能听懂的稳定语言解释扩展权衡。

steps.zh: 客户希望响应低于一秒。

focus.en: Ask whether the task truly needs generative reasoning at request time.
focus.zh: 先问这个任务是否真的需要在请求时做生成式推理。

steps.zh: 工具调用占据主要延迟。

focus.en: Talk about parallelism, caching, and orchestration shape before model choice.
focus.zh: 先谈并行、缓存和编排形态，再谈模型选择。

steps.en: The prototype is cheap, but production projections look expensive.
steps.zh: 原型很便宜，但生产成本预测很高。

focus.en: Move from cost per call to cost per successful task.
focus.zh: 从单次调用成本转到成功任务成本。

title.zh: AI 的 token 投资回报
